learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 550 kPa and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Initial 20 C gauge was 220 kPa. Keyboard Home gave 0 C and 198 kPa; End gave 60 C and 264 kPa. After-drive preset gave 50 C and 253 kPa, enabling reveal.
observations.reveal: Corrected to 253 kPa and distinguished 15 percent gauge rise from 10 percent absolute pressure rise. Explained kelvin 293 to 323 and total pressure 321 to 354, subtracting outside 101.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshot inspected. Stacked outside-air and pink gauge bar, dashed cold level, Celsius-to-kelvin label and total/gauge readings were legible above explanation.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner stated history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Choices expose both Celsius-ratio and total-pressure confusions.

interaction.reason: Reversible temperature range updates gauge and absolute labels.

payoff.reason: Reveal accounts for both offsets behind the answer.

clarity.reason: Stacked bar visually separates total from gauge pressure.
clarity.evidence: Outside-air base with gauge segment and dashed baseline.

transfer.reason: General pressure-temperature rule has explicit fixed-volume context but no new application.
transfer.evidence: Rigid sealed tyre and ideal gas label.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard endpoints worked; screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: A 2.5-fold Celsius number produces only 15 percent gauge rise.

visualExplanation.reason: Offset bar and temperature conversion show both corrections.

practicalValue.reason: Everyday gauge reading gains a scale explanation.

depth.reason: Combines absolute temperature and pressure reference offsets.

complexity.reason: Familiar object supports two unfamiliar zero-reference corrections.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Use absolute temperature ratios and distinguish total from gauge pressure.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Kelvin and gauge pressure introduced with visible offsets.

caveat: Rigid fixed volume and sealed ideal gas assumptions limit the example; no fresh application was tested.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
